comments.author: @ml1049
comments.text: Only in our culture is living with your parents past age 18-20 frowned upon. It's normal in other countries for families to cohabitate in the same household, often having multiple generations under the same roof. We have never had much money. We couldn't really help our two kids with college but they both got loans and went. Now they are in their thirties and still live with us because this is the one thing we can do for them, give them the opportunity to save money to eventually get a house of their own. We have no problems. We all get along, everyone pitches in with housework and they contribute to groceries. Both are single with no children. I have never had an issue with our adult children living with us, so I was surprised to find out from a friend that other people in our group thought that we should "kick them out and make them fend for themselves". Well, I'm sorry but in reality that would probably mean putting our daughter out on the street because despite her degree, she doesn't make enough money to rent an apartment on her own. How could I sleep at night knowing that she was sleeping in her car? Not all situations or families are the same. Children are not failures because they still live at home, society is failing them. The government is failing them. They need more help than we did at their age because of circumstances that are out of their control. People need to stop judging others.
